claim.summary: On a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a finite field, genus g, n distinct received rational points plus protected R, divisors A,G of degrees a,m>=0 avoiding all points, L received words from L(G) with exact error supports E_j, union size u and maximum size t: if a>=u+2g and n>a+m+t, actual error actions on common U=L(A) and their observed maps modulo ev L(A+G) have individual ranks |E_j| and joint rank u; their common kernel evaluates surjectively at R. One common normalized locator is found from the received words and recovers every message, in O(Ln^3) field operations and O(n^2+Ln) memory with bases/evaluations supplied. On Hermitian curves s=2^r>=8, n=s^3-1,g=s(s-1)/2,m=s^3/4-1,d=s^3/16-1,a=3d+2g, supports I union J and I union K for disjoint d-sets give ranks 2d,2d, joint 3d and incomparable kernels. The summed-rank criterion for a nonzero common multiplier first holds at pole order 4d+g (for every support choice when s>=16; with support-based rank bounds at s=8); a nonzero common multiplier exists at 3d+g and a protected one at a, savings d and d-g, with both windows feasible. Joint rank is union size by definition here; separate per-word locators are cheaper; no bound on paid PC errors or hardness transfer.

claim.summary: On a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a finite field, genus g, n distinct rational evaluation points, divisors A,G of nonnegative degrees a,m avoiding those points, t>=0, a>=t+g and n>a+m+t, recover any f in L(G) from its evaluations corrupted at <=t unknown positions. Solve N(P_i)=lambda(P_i)y_i with lambda in L(A), N in L(A+G). Nonzero solutions exist, every nonzero solution has lambda nonzero and N=lambda f identically, and kills every actual error. A second weighted evaluation system uniquely recovers f. If rational R avoids the points and supports of A,G and a>=t+2g, add lambda(R)=1; the system remains consistent and N(R)=f(R). With bases/evaluation matrices supplied, O(n^3) field operations and O(n^2) memory. Costs of producing those inputs are separate. This supplies geometric certificates for established bilinear error recovery, not a new decoder or a bounded-PC identification.

claim.summary: For a binary degree-D Boolean pseudoideal J, incoming weight w of degree<=b, candidate space U within degree<=K and actual error families E_alpha of degree<=e at b+K+e<=D, let V=U/{f:wf in J}, H=dim V, and K_alpha be the kernel of [f]->([wfE]_E). For two families of partial states with a common fixed compatible boundary and combined errors given by union, existence of a common surviving weighted annihilator is exactly K_alpha intersect K_beta nonzero. Its 0/1 matrix factors over F2 by C(alpha,v)=1_(v in K_alpha), columns nonzero v in V, hence rank<=2^H-1. Equivalently the two annihilator spaces in V* fail to span V*.
